title: Confirm
description: Asks the user to confirm an action: a themed replacement for window.confirm. Use the declarative ConfirmDialog or await confirm() from anywhere; with a ConfirmProvider the dialog renders inside your app tree, without one a standalone host is mounted on demand, and on the server confirm() resolves false.

usage.title: When to use which: useConfirm() or confirm()
usage.hook: Inside components, call useConfirm(): its dialogs follow the nearest ConfigProvider scope. Under a nested provider the modal portals into its host, with its theme, palette and tokens, and the default button labels use its language. A ConfirmProvider still renders them when there is one.
usage.function: Outside React (event buses, API clients, router guards and other non-component modules), import confirm() directly: no hook is available there, and its dialogs use the root theme and language.

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the dialog is open (controlled).

props.name: title
props.description: Title (the dialog's accessible name).

props.name: description
props.description: Explanation below the title (the dialog's accessible description).

props.name: confirmLabel
props.description: Label of the confirm button; defaults to the localized "Confirm", or "Delete" for `color="danger"`.

props.name: cancelLabel
props.description: Label of the cancel button; defaults to the localized "Cancel".

props.name: closeLabel
props.description: Accessible label of the close (×) button; defaults to the localized "Close".

props.name: color
props.description: Semantic color of the confirm button; `danger` marks a destructive action (and defaults its label to "Delete")

props.name: loading
props.description: Shows a spinner on the confirm button and disables cancel (e.g. while an async `onConfirm` runs)

props.name: confirmDisabled
props.description: Natively disables the confirm button (removes it from the tab order). While `loading` alone it stays focusable but cannot be activated again

events.name: onOpenChange
events.description: Called with `false` when the user cancels (cancel button, close, Escape, overlay click).

events.name: onConfirm
events.description: Called when the confirm button is pressed. The dialog does not close by itself.

examples.title: Colors
examples.description: color sets the tone of the confirm button: primary (default), warning, or danger for destructive actions (its label then defaults to "Delete"). The cancel button is always a neutral outline button.

examples.title: Declarative ConfirmDialog
examples.description: Controlled dialog; loading shows a spinner and locks cancel while onConfirm runs.

examples.title: Imperative confirm()
examples.description: await confirm({...}) resolves true when confirmed and false when cancelled (button, Escape or backdrop). No provider needed.

examples.title: With ConfirmProvider
examples.description: useConfirm() returns a confirm rendered by the provider (inside the caller's ConfigProvider scope), so dialogs share your app's context. Concurrent requests are shown one at a time.

examples.title: Scoped: useConfirm() vs confirm()
examples.description: Both buttons sit in a nested ConfigProvider (dark theme, tech palette, Chinese). useConfirm() opens its dialog inside that scope (dark tokens, Chinese button labels); confirm() opens it at the root, with the page theme and language.

basic.title: Basic usage
basic.description: A declarative <minerva-confirm-dialog> opened with show(). color="danger" marks a destructive action; minerva-confirm and minerva-cancel (with its reason) report the answer.

async.title: Async confirmation
async.description: onConfirm may return a promise: the Confirm button shows its loading state until it settles, and a rejection keeps the dialog open. Extra content goes in the default slot.

imperative.title: Imperative confirm()
imperative.description: confirm({ title, ... }) appends a dialog, resolves true or false and removes it once closed: a themed replacement for window.confirm. Concurrent calls are queued. Without a host and without a <minerva-confirm-provider>, the dialog is appended to document.body (root theme and language).

scoped.title: Scoped confirm and provider
scoped.description: confirm({ host }) (or confirmFor(host)) is the equivalent of useConfirm(): the dialog renders inside the host's <minerva-config> scope (dark, tech palette, Chinese labels) and is queued by the closest <minerva-confirm-provider>. confirm() without a host renders in the provider's own scope (here the root theme and language), like the global confirm().

props.label: Title (or use the header slot); names the dialog.

events.minerva-confirm: The Confirm button was pressed; cancelable: preventDefault() keeps the dialog open (close it yourself).
events.minerva-cancel: The confirmation was cancelled and the dialog closed (detail: { reason }).
events.minerva-open-change: The user asked to close (detail: { open, reason }); cancelable: preventDefault() keeps it open.
events.minerva-after-open: Fired once the panel is open and focus has moved in.
events.minerva-after-close: Fired once the panel has finished closing (after its exit animation).

slots.default: Optional extra content below the description.

cssVars.--modal-width: Width of the panel (defaults to the width of the size, capped by the viewport).
cssVars.--modal-max-height: Maximum height of the panel (the body scrolls beyond).
cssVars.--modal-padding: Horizontal padding of the header, description, body and footer.
cssVars.--modal-radius: Corner radius of the panel (defaults to --radius-xl).
cssVars.--modal-z-index: Stacking order of the panel (defaults to --z-modal).

props.confirm: Asks for a confirmation rendered by this provider (its scope, or the scope of options.host); resolves true when confirmed (read-only).

slots.default: Application content: confirm({ host }) / confirmFor(host) calls from inside are queued here.
